recipes.name: Dave's Georgia Black-Eyed Peas
ingredients_raw: 1 pound cooked ham, cut into bite-size pieces
salt and black pepper to taste

steps.text: Rinse, pick over, and place peas in a large bowl. Cover with several inches of cool water; let stand 8 hours to overnight. Drain and rinse.
Pour water into a large saucepan or stockpot. Add bouillon cubes and bring to a boil, stirring occasionally to dissolve bouillon. Stir in peas; reduce heat and bring to a simmer.

Place bacon in a large, deep skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain bacon slices on a paper towel-lined plate. Crumble bacon and set aside.
Melt butter in the pan with bacon grease; cook and stir onions until they begin to turn brown at the edges, about 10 minutes.
Stir onions and cooking fat into peas; add crumbled bacon, ham, salt, and pepper to taste. Simmer over low heat for 8 hours, stirring every hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Dave's Georgia Black-Eyed Peas
raw_recipe.description: This tasty black-eyed peas recipe involves cooking the black-eyed peas low and slow with bacon, onion, and ham. Serve with cornbread for a hearty meal.

review.reviewBody: I have never left a review on anything, but MAN these peas were that good. I used the recipe as written except I halfed it can only cooked it 4 hours due to less ingrediants and they were amazing! We lost my grandad this past year and it was his new years peas we gathered around every year, now my family has elected me to carry on that tradition! They were that good! :)

My whole life we have always been made to eat black eyed peas on New Years day, and I have always hated them! My parents would always just open a can of black eyed peas, heat them in the microwave and serve.. it's no wonder I hated them! So I decided to make these peas and now I must say that I love black eyed peas!! This recipe was awesome, the only changes I made was to cut it in half (I was only feeding 2.5 people so we didn't need a lot) I used 12 oz. of bacon because I didn't want to use just a partial package and I added a bit of garlic. I also cooked it in the crock pot on low for 4 hours and then on high for 4 hours. My husband even took these to have as a meal at work the next day. I will never go back to canned black eyed peas again :)

Excellent!! This recipe also works very well in the crock pot on low! Everyone that I have served this to has loved it. I have substituted pinto beans for the peas with equally good results. I do add 1-2 chopped jalepenos (you can deseed and soak the peppers in cool water for 10 minutes or so to reduce their heat) and some fresh minced garlic halfway through the onions' cook time.

I did the basic recipe but wanted to use my instant pot. Here’s what I did: I used (3) 1 lb bags of frozen black eyed peas. Just put them in the pot with 48 Oz of low sodium chicken broth. On the stove I cooked 1 1/2 lb of peppered bacon bits and pieces until crisp. Drain on a paper towel and crumble into pot. In the bacon grease add 1 stick butter and two chopped sweet onions and two chopped cloves of garlic. Once done transfer into pot. Add 1 lb of ham hocks. I use the smaller ones sold in bulk...not the meat department’s usual stock. For seasoning I used fresh ground black pepper, Crazy Jane’s Mixed Up Salt, low sodium Mediterranean spiced sea salt, smoked salt and a dash of cayenne pepper. It cooked on the bean setting for 45 minutes. I served with collard greens for money.

I made this recipe, and it is an excellent way of transforming a regular pot of black-eyed peas into a main dish. The onions sautéed in butter is a great way to add a hearty deep flavor to your dish.

A few tweaks I used were, adding a tablespoon of diced garlic to the onions, using chicken stock instead of bullion, and finishing off with a pinch of smoked paprika to taste (1 tsp. for me).

Really good. I made a half recipe and still have plenty leftover. I also used smoked turkey breast instead of ham and cooked it in a slow cooker after all the pre-cooking. My husband and I both loved it.

Here are a couples changes I made: 1) I didn't add in the ham, because I didn't have any more leftover from Christmas- I did, however, use a couple slices of hog jowl; 2) Used beef bouillon cubes instead of chicken.

 I ended up adding about 1 cup of water during cooking so they weren't so thick. I also didn't need to cook for the full 8 hours; I'd say that these were finished in about half the time. They were amazing! Definitely going to prepare these again next year!

Peas have a subtle flavor all their own and are best enjoyed without spices that take away from that flavor. Cover peas in water and add salt as if you were salting them on your plate. Add sliced dry salt meat or smoked pig knuckles. Bring to a boil in a covered pot and reduce heat to a slow simmer. After simmering for one hour, remove the lid and increase heat to bring it back to a simmer for 30 minutes. This is very important to allow the liquid to develop the color and rich flavor that really takes this dish from the mundane to the richness that takes it to the level of a culinary masterpiece. Forget all the herbs for this dish. It is so much more delicious without them.

I fixed this on New Year's Day and it was sooo good. Cooking the bacon and then the onions and then adding it to the beans made them so flavorful. The only change I made was I used chicken stock in place of the water and bouillon cubes. This is a keeper!

This was some of the very best black eyed peas I have ever eaten. I don’t normally care for them…..but it was new years and hubby likes tradition soooo. His mom would make them and he says they were better than hers. Here is what I did differently. Omitted the bacon. Used a meaty hambone left over from Thanksgiving. Soaked the beans for eight hours and then put them (along with the other ingredients) in the slow cooker on low overnight. By noon they were fantastic. Perfect with greens and corn bread.
Fantastic & easy. Put everything in the crockpot this morning (cooked on low for 10 hrs). I did add chopped carrots and celery, 1/2 cup each.

This recipe was phenomenal!! Only thing I did different was cut the recipe in half and then after I followed the first part, I put everything in my slow cooker on low for 7 hours then turned up to high for the last hour. The worst part was being home and having to smell it ALL DAY!! We loved it!!!

How could I have been eating canned Black Eyed Peas all these years?? After trying this recipe once, I can guarantee you I will never buy another canned Black Eyed Pea in my life. I have made so many of Nicole’s recipes and have not met one yet that did not turn out absolutely fabulous.
This is delicious! I was hesitant about the butter but it really enhanced the flavor. The only change I made was that I added a couple of sprinkles of dried jalapeno flakes.
I agree with ChristyMC. The only change I make is... I swap the ham for little smokies and bake some semi-sweet corn bread.
This was amazing I made no changes. My only question is how would I can these? Thanks for the recipe!
Great recipe! I cut the ingredients in half as I used a 1# bag. I used chicken broth in lieu of the bouillon since I didn't have any. It was very tasty!
